blocks.heading: Six Jobs Under One Name
rows: Cloud networking engineer (AWS or Azure virtual networks, hybrid links)
Builds and fixes virtual networks, private links to offices, firewalls and load balancers in the cloud, often through code.
Second job for most people. Needs routing basics first, then a cloud account you have actually built in.
Scalable
Cloud networking skills sell as project work and consulting, and the same skill moves across employers.
Network security engineer (firewalls, VPN, segmentation)
Writes and reviews firewall rules, secures remote access, and checks that a change does not open a hole.
Usually after a year or two as a network engineer.
Scalable with a business layer
Firewall reviews and managed security for small firms can be sold as a service. See the security guide for the wider lane.
Enterprise network engineer (switching, routing, Wi-Fi in an office or campus)
Keeps a company's wired and wireless network running, plans upgrades, and handles outages.
Entry through support, NOC or a junior engineer post.
Scalable with a business layer
A salaried ladder with fixed grades. It grows when you add automation and design skill, or serve small offices yourself.
SD-WAN and WAN engineer at an integrator or managed service provider
Connects many branch offices, banks' outlets or stores over broadband and leased lines, and manages them from one console.
Integrators and managed service providers hire juniors who have lab proof.
Scalable with a business layer
Repeatable rollouts across many sites. Ownership comes through a small managed-service business.
Telecom, ISP and 5G network engineer (core, transport, radio)
Runs the networks of mobile and broadband operators and the vendors that build them. Much of it is vendor-specific.
Telecom degree or diploma, vendor training and a fixed-ladder employer.
Not so scalable
Few employers, large equipment and licences, and little room to run your own version. Keep a transferable skill beside it.
NOC or network support (watching dashboards, raising and fixing tickets)
Monitors links and devices, follows a runbook, escalates what it cannot fix. Often in shifts.
The widest door for freshers, including diploma, BSc and BCA holders.
Not so scalable
Routine work with a low ceiling and the most automation pressure. Use it as a paid bridge, not a destination.

blocks.heading: What They Cost and What They Prove
rows: Cisco CCNA (exam 200-301)
About US$300 for one 120-minute exam. Cisco lists no requirement.
You can configure and troubleshoot a small network and you have met automation and security basics.
The exam fee is in dollars, so the rupee cost moves with the exchange rate. It does not prove you can run a live network.
Cisco CCNP Enterprise
Core exam ENCOR US$400, plus one concentration exam at US$300 (choices include SD-WAN, automation and secure cloud connectivity). No requirement listed.
Depth in design, routing and one specialty.
Valid three years. Worth it once a job gives you real devices to work on, not before.
Microsoft Azure Network Engineer Associate (AZ-700)
100-minute exam, price set by country. Renewal is free through an online assessment, and the page lists a 12 month renewal cycle.
You can design and manage Azure networks, assuming you already know names, protocols and addressing.
A good second certificate after CCNA, once you have built something in Azure.
AWS Advanced Networking Specialty
US$300, 170 minutes. AWS recommends five or more years of networking experience.
Senior cloud networking knowledge.
AWS says the last day to take this exam is 31 December 2026. Check what replaces it before you plan around it.
Juniper JNCIA-Junos
Check the official Juniper page for the current fee and exam code. Third-party sites disagree.
Junos basics, useful where an employer runs Juniper gear.
Pick it only if your target employers use Juniper. CCNA is the more common first ask.

blocks.heading: Pay, From Named Sources
rows: Entry level, under 1 year
Average total pay about Rs 2.95 lakh a year (181 salaries)
Most freshers start here. A certificate helps you get shortlisted. It does not by itself raise this number.
Early career, 1 to 4 years
Average total pay about Rs 4.13 lakh a year (299 salaries)
The first jump comes when you move from watching to changing the network.
All experience levels, base pay
Average about Rs 4.79 lakh. The 10th to 90th percentile runs from about Rs 2.4 lakh to Rs 10 lakh (491 profiles)
The spread is wide, so employer type and skill matter more than the title.
United States, for comparison
Median US$99,130 a year for network and systems administrators (US Bureau of Labor Statistics, May 2025)
A different market and currency. Do not read it as an Indian pay level.

blocks.heading: Entry Routes, Rated
rows: Class 12 or any graduate: CCNA preparation on free simulator practice, then a NOC or support job
Not so scalable
Fast and cheap to start. The role is routine, and the next climb (engineer, then design) is a separate filter.
Learn one change you can automate every month so you can leave the queue.
Diploma in electronics, computer or IT, then a junior network or telecom job
Scalable with a business layer
Practical diplomas fit installation and support work. Pay follows a fixed ladder at first.
Add automation and cloud basics, or serve small offices with cabling and Wi-Fi on the side.
BCA or BSc (IT, computer science, electronics)
Scalable with a business layer
The most common route into support and junior engineer posts, with room to move toward cloud and security.
Build a home lab and one documented project in the first year of work.
B.Tech in electronics and communication or computer science
Scalable with a business layer
Opens telecom, product and vendor roles and campus recruiting, but the degree alone is crowded.
Keep the college fee near 10% of the family education budget and spend the rest on lab, cloud practice and projects.
Skills first: lab proof plus cloud networking and Python, then a role or direct client work
Scalable
You control the pace. Proof can be shown to employers or sold to small clients.
Needs a clear offer, referrals and a price conversation. See the section on who pays.

blocks.heading: Who Should Skip, or Choose Another Door
rows: You want regular daytime hours with no call at all
Outages and upgrades happen outside office hours. The US labour bureau also notes that administrators may need evenings, nights or weekends.
You think one CCNA badge is the plan
Many people hold it. What separates candidates is a lab you can explain and a skill beyond typing commands.
You dislike troubleshooting with no clear answer
Most of the job is finding which of five possible causes is real, often while someone is waiting.
You want fast, high pay in the first role
Entry pay data shows an average near Rs 3 lakh for under one year. Big jumps usually come with a second job and a rarer skill.
You will not touch code
You can still do design, wireless or cabling work. But repeating manual commands is the part tools are taking.

items.text: Typing the same configuration on one device after another by hand.
Reading a log line by line to find which link dropped.
Drawing and updating diagrams manually after each change.
Who pays: the owner or manager of a small business, a builder, an interior designer, or a school administrator.
How they trust you: referrals from electricians, builders and IT shops, plus before-and-after photos and a neat network diagram.
First skill to learn: a simple offer and a site-visit quote.
One number to watch: how many site visits turn into signed quotes, and how many clients renew.
Standard configuration drafts and templated scripts.
First-line alert sorting and log summaries.
